neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Somewhat flat affect. Denies depressed mood but scores positive on PHQ-9.
neurological_exam.motor: Whole-body tremor — arms, legs, and trunk. Tremor frequency varies 3-7 Hz and changes when examiner asks patient to count backward from 100. Tremor stops when patient engages in a secondary task. POSITIVE tremor entrainment: when examiner asks patient to tap right hand at 2 Hz, the left hand tremor slows to match 2 Hz (entrainment sign = functional tremor).
neurological_exam.sensory: Diffuse non-anatomical tingling complaints but no objective sensory loss.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose: mild inaccuracy during tremor episode but normal between episodes.
neurological_exam.gait: Slow, wide-based during tremor episode. Normal gait between episodes when unaware of being observed.
neurological_exam.additional: Distractibility of tremor with cognitive tasks. Tremor present at rest and with action but with identical frequency range — organic essential tremor is typically either rest OR action.

patient.chief_complaint: Whole-body tremor and episodes of unresponsiveness — 6 weeks duration
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. B is a 41-year-old administrative assistant from a medical office who was admitted after being brought to the emergency department by her sister following a 6-week history of progressively worsening whole-body tremor and two episodes of unresponsiveness at home. The tremor began approximately 6 weeks ago, shortly after she was laid off from her job. It initially involved her right hand and has since spread to involve both arms, legs, and trunk. She describes the episodes as coming in waves, sometimes lasting minutes to hours, with relative periods of improvement in between. She has fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome and is familiar with the health system, having worked in a medical office. She has experienced panic disorder for several years but reports that the current tremor feels different from her usual panic attacks. The two episodes of unresponsiveness were described by her sister as lasting 2-3 minutes with closed eyes, no rhythmic limb movement, and immediate recovery with no confusion afterward. She denies any history of epilepsy or prior neurological conditions. She denies substance abuse. She is worried about Parkinson's disease because her neighbor was recently diagnosed. She has no family history of movement disorders or epilepsy.

mri.impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural or signal abnormality. No basal ganglia or substantia nigra pathology. Normal study, excluding Parkinson's disease and structural tremor causes. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.description: Normal symmetric 9 Hz posterior dominant rhythm. Well-formed background.

findings.morphology: NO EEG CHANGE during entire unresponsive episode. Normal continuous background throughout. No ictal pattern. Gamma band enhancement briefly during eye flutter — consistent with voluntary activity.

eeg.impression: Normal EEG. Unresponsive episode captured with NO EEG CORRELATE. Epileptic seizure excluded. Resistance to eye opening and closed eyes during episode support non-epileptic origin (epileptic patients cannot voluntarily close eyes during seizure). Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.morphology: No EEG change throughout entire tremor episode. Normal background. No rhythmic EEG correlate of tremor (organic tremor visible on EEG as rhythmic artifact; this tremor shows no EEG artifact).

output.impression: No EEG correlate of tremor episode. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions: Duloxetine: CYP1A2 consideration — minimal clinical interaction at current doses
warnings: Benzodiazepines (alprazolam) can perpetuate and worsen FND by promoting avoidance behaviors — gradual taper is appropriate in FND management
Taper should be slow (10-25% per 2 weeks) to avoid withdrawal seizures
alternatives: Buspirone for anxiety if alprazolam withdrawn

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Functional neurological disorder — functional tremor and PNES, with comorbid fibromyalgia and panic disorder

differential.key_feature: Functional tremor entrains to imposed external rhythm; organic essential tremor has fixed frequency; tremor stops with distraction — organic tremor does not disappear with distraction
Normal DaTscan (normal dopaminergic terminals); no rigidity; no bradykinesia; normal gait between episodes; tremor not rest-predominant with classic pill-rolling quality; MRI normal basal ganglia
Normal ceruloplasmin and urine copper; patient is 41 years old (Wilson's typically presents under age 40); no hepatic disease
Video-EEG shows no EEG correlate during episode; closed eyes, resistance to eye opening, and immediate full recovery are incompatible with epileptic seizure

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain — exclude structural tremor causes and basal ganglia disease
Video-EEG with tremor and episode capture
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No EEG correlate — functional tremor and PNES confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Labs — thyroid, ceruloplasmin, urine copper (Wilson's), prolactin post-event
optimal_actions.expected_finding: All normal — metabolic and toxic tremor causes excluded

optimal_actions.action: DaTscan — formally exclude Parkinson's disease (given patient concern)

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Severe depression, panic, three identified stressors

critical_actions: Document tremor distractibility and entrainment (positive functional signs)
contraindicated_actions: Initiating dopaminergic medication without dopamine deficit confirmation
Prolonged benzodiazepine prescription which perpetuates FND
key_reasoning_points: Tremor entrainment (frequency changes to match externally imposed rhythm) and distractibility are POSITIVE diagnostic signs for functional tremor
DaTscan is appropriate when patient is concerned about Parkinson's disease — normal result definitively excludes parkinsonism and helps patient accept FND diagnosis
Alprazolam (benzodiazepine) is counter-productive in FND management — avoidance behavior reinforcement; gradual taper recommended
Fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome are frequent comorbidities in FND — do not confuse co-existing somatic symptom disorder with FND

red_herrings.data_point: Patient works in medical office and has fibromyalgia/CFS (high medical utilizer)
red_herrings.location: Social history and past medical history
red_herrings.intended_effect: Label patient as 'functional' too quickly based on history alone without examining positive signs
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: FND diagnosis requires positive clinical signs (entrainment, distractibility, Hoover) — history alone does not diagnose FND

metadata.notes: Straightforward FND with functional tremor and PNES. DaTscan confirms no Parkinson's. Alprazolam taper important.
